chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon him), who said:
Beware of debt, for it is a humiliation during the day and a burden/stress during the night, and it requires payment in this world and payment in the Hereafter.
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and worldly consequences of debt according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) warns against incurring debt, describing it as a source of daily humiliation and nightly anxiety. The narration emphasizes that debt carries consequences in both the worldly life and the Hereafter, requiring repayment in both realms. In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith underscores the spiritual peril of financial obligation, linking the physical burden of repayment with the metaphysical weight of accountability on the Day of Judgment.
